value._status: CLOSED DEFINE — rationale drafted by tushar-patel28, 2026-10-01
value._what: Keyword crosswalk from sponsored job titles to three role families. The sponsorship data has no SOC field, so this file IS the definition of 'a title in this family'. It is not a record.
_rationale: Precision over recall. A keyword only maps a title to a family when the title clearly belongs there.
Ambiguous titles map to no family — e.g. Data Engineer, Solutions Architect, bare 'Engineer'. These count as 'not in top titles (unknown)'.
A match is a title match only. It verifies nothing about the visa's job category (SOC).
Known limitation: AI roles filed as 'Software Engineer' are invisible (prediction P1).
value._match_rule: A title belongs to a family when it matches NO exclude_patterns entry AND at least one of the family's patterns (case-insensitive, Python re.search). A title can belong to more than one family (e.g. 'Software Engineer, Machine Learning' is SWE and AI).

_changes_2026-10-01.added: exclude_patterns: manager/director/exec titles, sales/support/success, product/program/project, QA/test, analyst, design, team lead, and the two ambiguous examples named in the rationale (data engineer; solutions architect/engineer)
_changes_2026-10-01.SWE: 'software engineer' now ends at a word boundary (no 'Software Engineering Manager'); back-end/front-end/full-stack/mobile now require engineer|developer (one word may sit between, e.g. 'Full Stack Java Developer'); 'member of technical staff' REMOVED (MTS covers research, ML and hardware roles); 'application developer' widened to 'applications? developer'; added '<engineer|developer> - back-end|front-end|full-stack' (e.g. 'Staff Engineer (Full Stack)')
_changes_2026-10-01.AI: bare 'machine learning', 'ml', 'ai', 'artificial intelligence', 'deep learning', 'nlp', 'computer vision' now require engineer|scientist|researcher (one qualifier word allowed, e.g. 'Machine Learning Software Engineer', 'Computer Vision Research Engineer'); 'applied scientist', 'research scientist' and 'data scientist' REMOVED (wet-lab, analytics and actuarial roles share these titles); added 'ai/ml|ai/ds engineer' and '<engineer> … machine learning|ml|ai' within 25 characters
_changes_2026-10-01.Cloud: bare 'cloud', 'devops', 'infrastructure', 'site reliability', 'kubernetes' now require a role noun; bare 'reliability engineer' REMOVED (hardware/manufacturing reliability) — only site/systems/database reliability engineer remain; added '<engineer> … cloud|infrastructure|devops' within 25 characters

value._context_soc_codes: SOC codes per family are used ONLY to look up BLS median wages as report context. They are not used to match titles and do not enter the score. 15-2051 (Data Scientists) stays in the AI wage context as the AI-adjacent code named in the brief, even though 'data scientist' titles no longer map to the AI family.

value._status: sponsorship, fit, timeline and next_action are CLOSED DEFINEs (rationale drafted by tushar-patel28, 2026-10-01). liveness is an assumption of the offline prototype; g4 is the human gate's contract. None of these values is a record.

sponsorship._why: Evidence state (G1 status x family check) -> scorer tier and p. Tier names are the ones role-scorer.mjs reads (soft_sponsorship_tiers = likely/possible/unknown). These p values mostly set an ORDERING (Likely > Possible > Unknown), not a measured probability.

matched-h1b+in-top-titles.why: A positive record in my family, but no filing year, no SOC, and possibly doubled counts. This is past practice, not current intent, so it stays below Proven.

matched-h1b+not-in-top-titles.why: The company sponsors, but my family isn't visible in a short top-titles list. Existing sponsorship setup puts it above zero; nothing ties it to my role, so it stays below 0.5. An ordering, not a measured probability.

matched-h1b+titles-unreadable.why: Same as above: the company sponsors, and no family claim can be read from its titles.

no-h1b-trace.why: No sponsorship evidence either way -> no sponsorship vote (unknown is not no; p=0 would assert non-sponsorship).

not-found.why: Company name did not match the data; may be a coverage or name-match gap -> no vote.

ambiguous.why: More than one row matches; picking one would be a guess -> no vote until a human resolves it.

fit._why: My priority list is a ranking, so equal steps are the least-assumption encoding. The top is below 1.0 because fit is my own statement, not a verified skills match. The floor is 0.6 because I'd accept all three families. Fit weighs 0.30, so a 0.1 step moves the score by 0.03: it breaks ties and can't outweigh sponsorship evidence.

timeline._why: Planning arithmetic, not immigration advice. days = role start date - EAD start date (day 0 = the EAD start itself). 0.5 is deliberately below the scorer's 0.6 'weak' threshold, so both risk bands get flagged.

bands.name: more-than-30-days-before
bands.why: too early to negotiate onto the EAD start

bands.name: 1-30-days-before
bands.why: start date must be negotiated to on or after the EAD start

bands.name: more-than-90-days-after
bands.why: past the 90-day unemployment allowance (assumption; confirm with the school's international office)

liveness._why: The offline prototype never calls the network. Liveness is ASSUMED open so the scorer can run; it is not checked. It counts as checked only for a role with an accepted G4 entry, whose liveness_checked_on date the human recorded after running the liveness command.

g4._why: The only path to Apply. A human checks public labor-filing records and the posting, then fills the overrides file. A complete, allowed entry becomes the scorer's override {decision: 'Apply', reason}. An LCA is evidence of an intent to file, not an approved visa.
refuse_when: a required field is missing or has the wrong type
the role's entity result is ambiguous or not-found
the role_id is unknown, duplicated in the file, or the role was not scored
a date is in the future

next_action._why: Likely -> tailor an application. Possible -> network: a conversation can confirm whether the company sponsors this role family. Unknown -> network: a conversation resolves sponsorship policy and an application can't; unknown is not no. Gated -> skip. The two 'blocked' outcomes are kept.
